the ensemble existed precisely to prevent one lucky seed being read as a stable result; for that one phase the fix reported n=1 six times
the rule fired on its own author: the first envelope written for the R4 benchmark declared sample_size 12 for 12 timing batches on ONE instance, and was rejected
observed_result.question_for_the_reviewer: Where does certifying sample size against distinct INPUT hashes misfire? A Monte-Carlo integration with one input and many seeds genuinely has n > 1 in a sense my rule denies. Is the rule too strong, or is the fix to separate 'distinct inputs' from 'independent draws' as two quantities?
observed_result.statement: Sample size is certified against DISTINCT input hashes, never against the length of the seed list. An envelope declaring n seeds whose inputs hash identically has effective n = 1, and verification fails if it claims more.

typed_remainders.comparison: a review binds a reading of an argument to a commit; it does not bind a number to a measurement, and it cannot promote this claim
